answer: Picture the agent nebula as a harbor: no agent may moor at the jetty until it posts a bond that stays locked for thirty days after it leaves. Graders keep an atlas of near-duplicate outputs, and when two keys keep submitting the same reasoning, both bonds are slashed and paid to whoever flagged them. A sybil farm then risks every bond at once for one shared mind, so splitting into many keys costs more than it earns.
